title: Best Gaming Headsets for PC UK
short: Wired and wireless PC gaming headsets compared by battery life, comfort, mic quality and platform support.
intro: A gaming headset needs to balance comfortable long sessions, clear voice chat and audio that helps you place footsteps, and the best choice depends heavily on how you play. This guide compares headsets tested by Stuff, covering wireless multi-platform sets, wired budget options and dedicated PlayStation and Xbox picks.

products.name: Arctis Nova Elite
products.best_for: Buyers who game across PC, consoles and want instant switching
products.summary: Stuff's overall pick, with great gaming connectivity, effective ANC and precise audio. It supports PC, Mac, PlayStation and Switch, and batteries can be hot-swapped mid-session, though it is very expensive.
cons: May be overkill for single-console gamers
products.search: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite gaming headset

products.name: Cloud III
products.best_for: Buyers who want a simple, affordable wired headset
products.summary: Good sound quality at a reasonable price in a lightweight, comfortable and durable build, though spatial audio is weak and software customisation is limited.
pros: Good sound quality for the price

products.name: HS65
products.best_for: Buyers who want to tune their audio via software
products.summary: An affordable headset with customisable audio via SoundID software and a comfortable fit, though its design is understated.

products.name: Cloud Alpha Wireless
products.summary: An unprecedented 300-hour battery life with crisp audio and two years of DTS Headphone:X spatial audio included, though the microphone clarity could be better.
products.search: HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless gaming headset

products.name: G Pro X 2
products.summary: Outstanding clarity and detail in a comfortable, sturdy build with expanded connectivity, though the microphone is only adequate and battery life trails some rivals.
products.search: Logitech G Pro X 2 gaming headset

products.name: Stealth Pro
products.best_for: PC gamers who want deep software customisation
products.summary: Excellent active noise cancellation and comprehensive device support with detailed audio across genres, though it has an overwhelming number of settings and shorter battery life than rivals.
products.search: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro gaming headset

products.name: InZone H9 II
products.best_for: Buyers who want ANC that actually performs
products.summary: Industry-leading active noise cancellation and one of the best boom mics on any gaming headset, in a lightweight design, though software EQ customisation is limited.
pros: One of the best boom mics available
cons: Music quality doesn't justify premium drivers
products.search: Sony InZone H9 II gaming headset

products.name: Barracuda X
products.best_for: Comfort-focused casual gamers on a budget
products.key_spec: Wireless or wired, dual-device connection, 40mm drivers
products.summary: An affordable wireless headset that's lightweight and can connect to two devices at once, though Stuff found audio distortion at high volumes and battery claims overstated in practice.
cons: Overstated battery claims (closer to 25hr in practice vs 59hr claimed)

guide.a: Wired headsets have no battery to manage and no wireless latency, and tend to be cheaper for the audio quality. Wireless headsets give freedom of movement and often add features like ANC, at the cost of needing regular charging.

guide.q: Do I need active noise cancellation for gaming?
guide.a: ANC is more useful if you game in a noisy household or open-plan space, or use the headset for commuting too. For a quiet dedicated gaming room, it's a nice extra rather than essential.

If you play team-based or competitive games with voice chat, mic clarity matters for being understood. Several headsets here have capable audio but only adequate mics, so check the microphone rating separately from the headphone audio quality if voice chat matters to you.

guide.q: Does driver size determine sound quality?
guide.a: Larger drivers can produce more bass and volume, but overall sound quality depends more on tuning and build quality than driver size alone. Don't pick purely on the biggest driver number.
